steps.prompt: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for 10 pancakes. Set up a ratio table with flour in the top row and pancakes in the bottom row. What pair do we know?
steps.reveal: Flour: 2 | Pancakes: 10. Every new column must keep this same flour-to-pancake relationship.

steps.prompt: We want the flour for 30 pancakes. What do we multiply 10 by to get 30?
steps.reveal: Multiply by 3. Whatever multiplies the bottom must multiply the top the same way: 2 x 3 = 6 cups of flour.

steps.prompt: Why can't we add instead? 10 + 20 = 30, so why isn't the answer 2 + 20 = 22 cups?
steps.reveal: Adding the same amount breaks the ratio: 22/30 is not equal to 2/10. Ratio tables scale by multiplying, never by adding the same number to both rows.

steps.prompt: Use the same table to find the flour for just 5 pancakes.
steps.reveal: 5 is 10 x 1/2, so the flour is 2 x 1/2 = 1 cup. Scaling down works the same way: multiply both rows by the same fraction.

workedExamples.title: Solving a Proportion with Equal Ratios

steps.prompt: Solve 3/4 = x/20. First, say what this proportion means in words.
steps.reveal: It says 3 out of every 4 is the same rate as x out of every 20. The two fractions must be the exact same ratio.

steps.prompt: Compare the bottoms: what multiplies 4 to give 20?
If the bottom was multiplied by 5, what must happen to the top?
steps.reveal: The top must be multiplied by the same 5 to keep the ratios equal: x = 3 x 5 = 15.

steps.prompt: Check the answer: is 15/20 really the same ratio as 3/4?
steps.reveal: Yes. Divide the top and bottom of 15/20 by 5 and you get back 3/4. Equal ratios always scale by the same factor.

p1.prompt: A batter has 12 hits in 48 at-bats. What is her rate of hits per at-bat?
hints: Hits per at-bat means hits divided by at-bats: 12 divided by 48.

p1.prompt: A batter has 9 hits in his first 30 at-bats. If he keeps hitting at the same rate, how many hits will he have after 60 at-bats?
hints: Set up a ratio table: 9 hits per 30 at-bats. 60 at-bats is double 30.
If the at-bats double, the hits double too — multiply, don't add.

p1.prompt: A team scores 35 runs over 7 games. How many runs per game is that?
hints: Runs per game means runs divided by games.
Keep the order: the thing being measured (runs) goes on top.

p1.prompt: A hitter has 27 hits in 90 at-bats — a .300 rate. At that same rate, how many hits would she have in 200 at-bats?
hints: First find the unit rate: 27 divided by 90 gives hits per single at-bat.
Then multiply that rate by 200 at-bats.

p1.prompt: A pitcher records 14 strikeouts in 7 innings. How many strikeouts per inning is that?
hints: Strikeouts per inning means strikeouts divided by innings.

p1.prompt: A softball team scores 24 runs in its first 6 games. At the same scoring rate, how many runs will it have after 10 games?
hints: Find runs per game first: 24 divided by 6.
Then multiply the per-game rate by 10 games.

p1.prompt: A catcher throws out 6 runners in 15 steal attempts. What is her throw-out rate per attempt?
hints: Rate per attempt means throw-outs divided by attempts: 6 divided by 15.
The answer should be less than 1 — she throws out fewer runners than there are attempts.

p1.prompt: A pitcher has 12 strikeouts over 8 innings. Pitching at that same rate, how many strikeouts will she have after 22 innings?
hints: Find strikeouts per inning: 12 divided by 8 is 1.5.
Multiply 1.5 strikeouts per inning by 22 innings.

p1.prompt: A player makes 20 of her 25 free throws. What is her rate of makes per attempt?
hints: Makes per attempt means makes divided by attempts: 20 divided by 25.

p1.prompt: A guard scores 45 points over his first 3 games. Scoring at that same rate, how many points will he have after 8 games?
hints: Find points per game first: 45 divided by 3.
Multiply that points-per-game rate by 8 games.

p1.prompt: A point guard has 40 assists in 16 games. How many assists per game is that?
hints: Assists per game means assists divided by games.
Keep the order: assists on top, games on the bottom.

p1.prompt: A forward has scored 110 points through 5 games. If she scores at the same rate all season, how many points will she have after 18 games?
hints: Find her points per game: 110 divided by 5.
Multiply that rate by 18 games — adding the extra games to her points doesn't keep the rate.

p1.prompt: A striker scores 12 goals in 24 matches. What is his goals-per-match rate?
hints: Goals per match means goals divided by matches: 12 divided by 24.

p1.prompt: A forward scores 5 goals in her first 10 matches. Scoring at the same rate, how many goals will she have over a 30-match season?
hints: 10 matches became 30 matches. What was 10 multiplied by?
Multiply the goals by that same number — don't add the extra matches.

p1.prompt: A goalkeeper makes 30 saves across 12 matches. How many saves per match is that?
hints: Saves per match means saves divided by matches.
The thing being counted (saves) goes on top.

p1.prompt: A striker has played 540 minutes this season and scored 3 goals. Coaches compare scorers using goals per 90 minutes. What is his goals-per-90 rate?
hints: First find how many full 90-minute blocks are in 540 minutes.
Then divide goals by the number of 90-minute blocks.

p1.prompt: A running back gains 120 yards on 24 carries. What is his yards-per-carry average?
hints: Yards per carry means yards divided by carries: 120 divided by 24.

p1.prompt: A running back gains 64 yards on his first 8 carries. Running at that same rate, how many yards will he have after 20 carries?
hints: Find yards per carry first: 64 divided by 8.
Multiply that rate by 20 carries — adding the extra carries to his yards breaks the rate.

p1.prompt: A quarterback completes 24 of his 30 passes. What is his rate of completions per attempt?
hints: Completions per attempt means completions divided by attempts.
The answer should be less than 1 — he completes fewer passes than he throws.

p1.prompt: A kicker has made 9 field goals in 12 attempts. Kicking at that same rate, how many field goals would he make in 28 attempts?
hints: Find his make rate per attempt: 9 divided by 12 is 0.75.
Multiply 0.75 by 28 attempts.

p1.prompt: An outside hitter records 44 kills across 11 sets. How many kills per set is that?
hints: Kills per set means kills divided by sets: 44 divided by 11.

p1.prompt: A hitter has 18 kills through 6 sets. Hitting at the same rate, how many kills will she have after 15 sets?
hints: Find kills per set first: 18 divided by 6.
Multiply that per-set rate by 15 sets.

p1.prompt: A defensive specialist makes 35 digs over 14 sets. How many digs per set is that?
hints: Digs per set means digs divided by sets.
The thing being counted (digs) goes on top.

p1.prompt: A server has landed 45 of her 50 serves in play. Serving at that same rate, how many serves will land in over her next 120 attempts?
hints: Find her in-serve rate: 45 divided by 50 is 0.9.
Multiply 0.9 by 120 attempts — don't add the extra attempts to her makes.

p1.prompt: Four granola bars cost $5.00. What is the cost per bar, in dollars?
hints: Cost per bar means total cost divided by the number of bars.

p1.prompt: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour to make 24 muffins. How many cups of flour are needed for 40 muffins?
hints: Find the flour per muffin first: 3 divided by 24.
Multiply that per-muffin amount by 40 muffins.

p1.prompt: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours at a steady speed. What is its speed in miles per hour?
hints: Miles per hour means miles divided by hours.
Steady speed is a unit rate: distance for one hour.

p1.prompt: At a market, 5 pounds of apples cost $6.00. At the same price per pound, how much do 8 pounds cost, in dollars?
hints: Find the price for one pound: 6 divided by 5.
Multiply the price per pound by 8 — adding the extra pounds to the price doesn't keep the rate.

p2.prompt: A batter's ratio of hits to at-bats is 9/30. Solve the proportion 9/30 = x/10 to find the hits expected in 10 at-bats.
hints: Both fractions must keep hits on top and at-bats on the bottom.
30 divided by 3 gives 10, so divide the top by 3 as well.

p2.prompt: A hitter bats at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. At-bats: 5, 15, 45. Hits: 2, 6, x. Find x.
hints: From 15 at-bats to 45 at-bats is multiplying by 3.
Multiply the hits by the same 3 — ratio tables scale by multiplying, not adding.

p2.prompt: A batter has 12 hits in 48 at-bats. Solve 12/48 = x/1 to find her hits-per-at-bat unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the same ratio scaled so the bottom is 1.
48 divided by 48 is 1, so divide 12 by 48 as well.

p2.prompt: A hitter's hits-to-at-bats ratio stays at 27/90 all season. Solve 27/90 = 45/x to find the at-bats needed to reach 45 hits.
hints: Here x is at-bats, on the bottom of the second ratio.
27/90 is a 0.3 hits-per-at-bat rate. How many at-bats does 45 hits take at 0.3 per at-bat?

p2.prompt: A pitcher has 14 strikeouts in 7 innings. Solve 14/7 = x/1 to find her strikeouts-per-inning unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom equals 1.

p2.prompt: A pitcher strikes out batters at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Innings: 4, 12, 24. Strikeouts: 6, 18, x. Find x.
hints: From 12 innings to 24 innings is multiplying by 2.
Multiply the strikeouts by that same 2 — don't add the difference.

p2.prompt: A base runner's ratio of successful steals to attempts is 3/4. Solve the proportion 3/4 = x/20 to find the steals expected in 20 attempts.
hints: What was 4 multiplied by to get 20?
Multiply the top by that same factor.

p2.prompt: A pitcher's strikeouts-to-innings ratio holds steady at 12/8. Solve 12/8 = 33/x to find the innings needed to reach 33 strikeouts.
hints: Here x is innings, on the bottom of the second ratio.
12/8 is 1.5 strikeouts per inning. How many innings does 33 strikeouts take at 1.5 per inning?

p2.prompt: A point guard has 40 assists in 16 games. Solve 40/16 = x/1 to find her assists-per-game unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom is 1: divide both parts by 16.

p2.prompt: A forward scores at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Games: 3, 6, 12. Points: 51, 102, x. Find x.
hints: From 6 games to 12 games is multiplying by 2.
Multiply the points by the same 2 — adding a pattern breaks the ratio.

p2.prompt: A center's ratio of free throws made to attempts is 20/25. Solve the proportion 20/25 = x/100 to find the makes expected in 100 attempts.
hints: What was 25 multiplied by to get 100?
Keep makes on top in both ratios, then multiply the top by the same factor.

p2.prompt: A guard's points-to-games ratio holds at 26/2 all season. Solve 26/2 = 91/x to find how many games it takes her to reach 91 points.
hints: Here x is games, on the bottom of the second ratio.
26/2 is 13 points per game. How many games does 91 points take at 13 per game?

p2.prompt: A striker has 12 goals in 24 matches. Solve 12/24 = x/1 to find his goals-per-match unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom is 1: divide both parts by 24.

p2.prompt: A forward scores at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Matches: 5, 10, 30. Goals: 2, 4, x. Find x.
hints: From 10 matches to 30 matches is multiplying by 3.
Multiply the goals by that same 3 — don't extend the pattern by adding.

p2.prompt: A winger's ratio of assists to matches is 3/5. Solve the proportion 3/5 = x/35 to find the assists expected over 35 matches.
hints: What was 5 multiplied by to get 35?
Multiply the top by that same factor.

p2.prompt: A striker scored 4 goals in 360 minutes of play. Coaches rate scorers in goals per 90 minutes. Solve 4/360 = x/90 to find his goals-per-90 rate.
hints: Keep goals on top and minutes on the bottom in BOTH ratios.
360 divided by 4 is 90, so divide the top by 4 as well.

p2.prompt: A running back has 160 yards on 40 carries. Solve 160/40 = x/1 to find his yards-per-carry unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom is 1: divide both parts by 40.

p2.prompt: A running back gains yards at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Carries: 4, 8, 24. Yards: 22, 44, x. Find x.
hints: From 8 carries to 24 carries is multiplying by 3.
Multiply the yards by that same 3 — adding the difference breaks the rate.

p2.prompt: A quarterback's ratio of completions to attempts is 18/24. Solve the proportion 18/24 = x/32 to find the completions expected in 32 attempts.
hints: 18/24 is a 0.75 completion rate.
Multiply 0.75 by 32 attempts — keep completions on top in both ratios.

p2.prompt: A receiver's ratio of receiving yards to catches holds at 96/8. Solve 96/8 = 132/x to find how many catches it takes to reach 132 yards.
hints: Here x is catches, on the bottom of the second ratio.
96/8 is 12 yards per catch. How many catches does 132 yards take at 12 per catch?

p2.prompt: An outside hitter has 36 kills in 9 sets. Solve 36/9 = x/1 to find her kills-per-set unit rate.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom is 1: divide both parts by 9.

p2.prompt: A hitter records kills at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Sets: 3, 9, 27. Kills: 12, 36, x. Find x.
hints: From 9 sets to 27 sets is multiplying by 3.
Multiply the kills by that same 3 — ratio tables scale by multiplying.

p2.prompt: A server's ratio of in-serves to attempts is 27/30. Solve the proportion 27/30 = x/40 to find the in-serves expected over 40 attempts.
hints: 27/30 is a 0.9 in-serve rate.
Multiply 0.9 by 40 attempts — don't add the extra attempts.

p2.prompt: A middle blocker's kills-to-sets ratio holds at 16/4. Solve 16/4 = 52/x to find how many sets it takes her to reach 52 kills.
hints: Here x is sets, on the bottom of the second ratio.
16/4 is 4 kills per set. How many sets does 52 kills take at 4 per set?

p2.prompt: Three pounds of grapes cost $7.50. Solve 7.50/3 = x/1 to find the price per pound, in dollars.
hints: A unit rate is the ratio scaled so the bottom is 1: divide both parts by 3.

p2.prompt: A pancake recipe scales at a steady rate. Complete the ratio table. Cups of flour: 2, 4, 12. Pancakes: 14, 28, x. Find x.
hints: From 4 cups to 12 cups is multiplying by 3.
Multiply the pancakes by that same 3 — adding a pattern breaks the ratio.

p2.prompt: A punch recipe uses 2 cups of juice for every 5 cups of sparkling water. Solve the proportion 2/5 = x/30 to find the cups of juice needed with 30 cups of sparkling water.
hints: What was 5 multiplied by to get 30?
Multiply the top by that same factor — don't add the difference.

p2.prompt: On a map, 5 centimeters represents 8 kilometers. Solve 5/8 = 35/x to find the real distance, in kilometers, represented by 35 centimeters.
hints: What was 5 multiplied by to get 35?
Multiply 8 by that same factor — both parts of a ratio scale together.
10 divided by 2 gives 5, so divide the top by 2 as well.

p3.prompt: An 18-ounce box of cereal costs $4.50. What is the price per ounce, in dollars?
hints: Price per ounce means total price divided by the number of ounces.
Keep the order: dollars on top, ounces on the bottom.
6/9 is the same ratio as 2/3.
Find the number that makes 10/x also equal to 2/3 — scale by multiplying, not by adding.

p3.prompt: A photo is 4 inches wide and 6 inches tall. It is enlarged so that the width becomes 14 inches. To keep the same shape, how tall must the enlargement be, in inches?
hints: Find the scale factor: what was 4 multiplied by to get 14?
Multiply the height by that same factor — adding 10 to both sides changes the shape.

p3.prompt: Mix A makes a shade of green using 4 cups of blue paint with 6 cups of yellow paint. Mix B uses 6 cups of blue paint. How many cups of yellow paint does Mix B need to make the exact same shade?
hints: The same shade means the same blue-to-yellow RATIO, not the same difference.
4 to 6 simplifies to 2 to 3. Scale 2 to 3 up until the blue part is 6.
36 divided by 3 gives 12, so divide 15 by 3 as well.
Check your answer: x/12 should simplify to the same ratio as 15/36.
